title: Architecture Graph architecture
scope: AG 0.3.1: declarations, context, interfaces and delivery. Software ownership is modeled; human assignments remain open. Excludes predecessor internals, explorer UI and implementation assurance.
limitation: Structural validation only; declarations and file existence do not prove implementation conformance.

unresolved.description: Open: Zod definitions in src/schema.ts generate the published JSON Schema today. A hand-written JSON Schema as the source would make the language-neutral contract authoritative for other readers such as a browser viewer, at the cost of rewriting working validation. Revisit when a viewer reads the published schema.

Modeling question: docs identify source responsibilities but do not assign human reviewers for schemas, public API and releases. Keep software ownership here; decide whether named maintainer/team ownership belongs in this graph or separate repository governance.

Open: docs record no successful live marketplace test. Choose routes after testing agent installation, discovery, updates/removal and coexistence with project copies. Claude manifests do not establish Codex compatibility.

Open: compatibility docs explicitly say Windows is untested and CI has no Windows job. Decide whether to add a supported Windows test target or continue documenting the gap; Node portability alone does not resolve it.
Determines which artifact is the authoritative definition of the authored format.
Schema-first would replace the Zod definitions with a hand-written schema and validator.
Public interface review responsibility is not assigned to a named person in this model.
Schema compatibility changes need a review owner if human governance is added to this record.
Project-copy installation is implemented; additional marketplace routes need live verification before readiness claims.
Adding a supported platform would require CI and packaged consumer evidence; current matrix leaves Windows untested.
